sections.h2: What Florida weather does to a Lake City deck
body: A deck sits flat under the sun and catches every rain shower, so it ages faster than anything else on the property. UV breaks down the wood fibers on top and turns them gray. Water soaks into end grain and fastener holes. Where the deck sits low and shaded, mildew and algae make the boards slick. Most of the decks we stain in Lake City subdivisions show all three by the time the owner calls. Deck staining in Lake City, FL reverses the surface damage and slows down what's happening underneath.

Stain will not save a soft board. Before we quote a stain job, the crew lead probes boards, stair treads, and rail posts and notes anything that needs replacing. Our article on signs of deck wood rot shows what we look for, so you can do a quick check yourself before the walkthrough.

Old stain that is peeling or flaking has to come off. Peeling film traps water, and new stain can't soak in through it. After stripping and cleaning, the deck dries before we sand away raised grain and gray fibers. Then a penetrating stain goes on. Sprayed areas are back-brushed so the stain works into the grain and gaps, not just onto the surface.
bullets: Board, tread, and loose fastener repairs

sections.h2: Choosing opacity and planning around the weather
body: A transparent stain shows the most grain but needs refreshing sooner. A solid stain hides more and lasts longer, but it acts more like paint. Semi-transparent is the most common middle ground. Stain needs dry wood and a dry forecast, so fall through spring is the easiest season. In summer, we work in the mornings and keep an eye on radar.

A deck usually sits beside a fence that needs the same treatment. Our Lake City fence staining crew can match the color. For general background, see our main deck and fence staining page, and the Lake City overview for everything else we do in town.

faqs.q: How often does a Lake City deck need restaining?
faqs.a: It depends on sun exposure and opacity. Transparent stains need refreshing sooner than solid ones. During the walkthrough, we look at how the current finish has worn and recommend an opacity based on that.

faqs.q: Can you stain over the old deck stain?
faqs.a: Only if the old stain is still sound and soaking in. Peeling or flaking coatings are stripped first so the new stain can penetrate.
Yes. Board, tread, and fastener repairs are noted during the walkthrough and listed on the estimate before staining.

faqs.q: When is the best time of year to stain a deck in Lake City?
faqs.a: Fall through spring, when there is less humidity and fewer afternoon storms. Summer jobs are done in the mornings, and only after the wood has dried out from the last rain.
